confirmed.title: attemptErrorCode logs UNCLASSIFIED for the codebase's own retryable failures and for AWS SDK exceptions
confirmed.evidence: The class-name branch only accepts names ending in 'Error' (/^(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,40})?Error$/). This codebase's own failures that are deliberately thrown out of handlers to fail and retry an attempt do not end in 'Error': ExportLoadFailed (reconcile/job.ts:58, the reconcile attempt's designed failure), DigestSendFailed (digest/job.ts:128), PricedOutOfOrder (price/execute.ts:378, after PRICING_TRANSACTIONS) and ReleaseTypeNotRead (price/release.ts:520). None carries an upper-case `code`. AWS SDK v3 S3 and KMS exceptions (name NoSuchKey, ThrottlingException, ...) likewise reach the same UNCLASSIFIED a non-object throw gets, so the line loses exactly the information it exists to give. Scratch test /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/e935a935-d2ff-5a27-860c-22677590c441/scratchpad/rev-wrk-scripts/zz-scratch-review.test.ts (run in the clone at c2626113) printed {"exportLoadFailed":"UNCLASSIFIED","digestSendFailed":"UNCLASSIFIED","releaseTypeNotRead":"UNCLASSIFIED","s3NoSuchKey":"UNCLASSIFIED","kmsThrottling":"UNCLASSIFIED"}.
confirmed.fix: Take the class's own name when `error instanceof Error && error.name === error.constructor.name` and it matches /^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,62}$/, converted to upper snake case (EXPORT_LOAD_FAILED, NO_SUCH_KEY). A name set by Object.assign ('Pat Doe', 'Smith') still fails the constructor check, so the existing PHI-guard test cases stay UNCLASSIFIED. Add these classes to the unit test.

confirmed.title: An attempt pg-boss expires (expireInSeconds) logs no `job attempt failed` line, though the doc comment and runbook say every failed attempt does
confirmed.evidence: pg-boss 12.38 fails an attempt at expireInSeconds from inside its own worker (manager.js:688 resolveWithinSeconds), and keeps the loop held until the abandoned handler returns. When that handler then resolves, attempt() takes its success path: no warn line, a 'job heap' line, and runJob records job_run 'succeeded' for an attempt pg-boss already failed. Scratch db test /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/e935a935-d2ff-5a27-860c-22677590c441/scratchpad/rev-wrk-scripts/zz-scratch-expiry.db.test.ts used a real PgBoss on 5433, a digest queue pre-created with expireInSeconds 1, and a first attempt sleeping 2.5 s. Result: the job completed with retry_count 1 after 2 handler calls; the logged lines were only [worker heartbeat, worker started, job heap, job heap], with zero 'job attempt failed'. This is the F reconcile 900 s case 068e8ed1's margin is about. The summary would then print '(its failed attempts logged no `job attempt failed` line)'. docs/runbooks/ci.md:76 says 'Each failed attempt logs `job attempt failed`' and gives no reading for its absence. JOB_ATTEMPT_FAILED_MESSAGE's doc (worker.ts:104-110) says the same.
confirmed.fix: In attempt(), after run() resolves, check whether pg-boss already failed the attempt. Its per-job job.signal is aborted when the batch times out, before the abandoned handler returns; it is aborted on ordinary completion only after attempt() returns. If so, log the warn line with a fixed code such as JOB_EXPIRED, and have runJob record 'retrying' rather than 'succeeded'. Alternatively, log the boss 'warning' HANDLER_OVERRUN event's job IDs with that code. Either way, say in ci.md what a missing line means (an expiry or a process restart).

confirmed.title: The Known gap margin reads only the last attempt, so an F reconcile whose first attempt expired is reported with time to spare, and the 'past its attempt' branch cannot fire
confirmed.evidence: knownGap uses F reconcile's elapsedMs, which run.ts:285 reads as completed_on - started_on. pg-boss resets started_on at every claim (plans.js:2558 `started_on = job_now()`), so it is the last attempt's duration. pg-boss also fails any attempt at 900 s, so a completed job's last attempt is always under 900 s and the `elapsedMs > attempt` branch (checks.ts:633) is unreachable in a real run. Evidence: (1) the db scratch test above read ms 8.0 for a job whose first attempt ran 2.5 s past a 1 s expiry. (2) A scratch unit test (text kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/e935a935-d2ff-5a27-860c-22677590c441/scratchpad/rev-wrk-scripts/checks-scratch-append.ts.txt) gave knownGap an F reconcile with attempts 2 and elapsedMs 600000. It printed 'This run's step 7b reconciled F's 2,000 lines in 600.0 s of its 900 s attempt (67%, 300.0 s to spare)', exactly when F's first attempt is the one that did not fit.
confirmed.fix: When F reconcile's attempts > 1, do not print a margin: say it completed on attempt N and that its earlier attempt did not complete within its 900 s attempt (with its logged codes, or none, which means an expiry). Or time F from its first claim, e.g. job_run's attempt-1 started_at or created_on to completed_on, less the retry delay. Add that form to the margin's tests.

confirmed.title: workerTaskPools undercounts the screening task's queue-login connections by pg-boss's LISTEN client
confirmed.evidence: pools.ts:11-15 counts pg-boss as QUEUE_POOL_CONNECTIONS (10), 'its fetches, completions, sends and maintenance'. The screening consumer's PgBoss is built with SCREENING_BOSS_OPTIONS { useListenNotify: true } (main.ts:111). pg-boss 12.38 then opens a dedicated pg.Client outside its pool for LISTEN (db.js:153-158: 'A separate pg.Client (not a pooled connection) is used so the listener never depletes the query pool'; db.js:239 new pg.Client). That is one more queue-login connection per screening task, two during a deploy, which infra/lib/connections.ts never counts. No environment's fit changes (production 207 vs 389).
confirmed.fix: Count the listener: a LISTEN_CONNECTIONS = 1 entry in workerTaskPools('screening'), labelled 'pg-boss LISTEN (queue login)'.

confirmed.title: The connection budget leaves out the screening consumer's pg-boss LISTEN/NOTIFY connection, so each screening task can hold 19 connections, not the 18 counted
confirmed.evidence: main.ts:111 starts the screening consumer's PgBoss with `max: QUEUE_POOL_CONNECTIONS` and `...SCREENING_BOSS_OPTIONS`, which is `{ useListenNotify: true }` (apps/worker/src/jobs/screening.ts:102). In pg-boss 12.38, the notifier (index.js:221, notifier.js:58) calls Db.listen. Db.listen opens 'a dedicated, session-pinned connection for LISTEN/NOTIFY. A separate pg.Client (not a pooled connection)' (node_modules/.pnpm/pg-boss@12.38.0*/dist/db.js:153-160, `new pg.Client` at :239), so the pool's `max` does not cap it. workerTaskPools('screening') at pools.ts:45-50 counts sweep 2 + threads 3x2 + pg-boss 10 = 18, and the QUEUE_POOL_CONNECTIONS comment (pools.ts:11-14) says pg-boss holds only its pool. Probe I ran (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/e935a935-d2ff-5a27-860c-22677590c441/scratchpad/rev1b-infra-probe/listen.mjs, against tp_sc1b_nr_1 on 5433, database dropped afterwards). It starts PgBoss with max 10 and fills the pool with 13 concurrent pg_sleep calls, then counts pg_stat_activity: `{"max":10,"useListenNotify":true,"backends":11,"listenerBackends":1}`; the same run without the option gave 10. The practice task (production: screening null, so no listener), the platform task and the web producer do not set the option, so only the screening task is affected. The true worst case is 2 x 19 for screening: 207 in production and 165 in dev and staging, not 205 and 163. Every environment still fits (389 available), and staging's former db.t4g.small fails by more (165 against 163), so the class decision holds. But the budget exists to be an exact sum, and the wrong figures are now pinned in the code, the test (infra/test/connections.test.ts:27-30, :88 `toBe(18)`, :122 message, :130 `worstCase: 163`), infra/lib/environments.ts:100-103, docs/runbooks/incident-response.md:122 ('205 in production, 163 in dev and staging') and ADR 0083 (line 660, 'pg-boss's 10, 18', and :671-673).
confirmed.fix: In workerTaskPools' screening case, add the listener as its own entry, e.g. `{ pool: 'pg-boss LISTEN/NOTIFY client (queue login, outside its pool)', connections: SCREENING_BOSS_OPTIONS.useListenNotify ? 1 : 0 }` (imported from ./jobs/screening, so turning the option off removes it). Correct the QUEUE_POOL_CONNECTIONS comment. Update connections.test.ts (screening 19, EXPECTED worstCase 165/165/207, the refusal message 'screening 2 x 19 ... 165 at once', the micro case's worstCase 165) and the figures in environments.ts, incident-response.md and ADR 0083.

confirmed.title: The incident runbook gives the budget's estimate of the refusal point (389) as the database's actual limit
confirmed.evidence: The runbook says 'Past 389 the database refuses new connections'. But 394 is connections.ts's deliberately low estimate of DBInstanceClassMemory (memory less max(512 MiB, 1/8), connections.ts:44-46). The commit's own source puts 4 GiB at 402 on PG17 (ADR 0083, around line 668; connections.test.ts:106), so a real db.t4g.medium most likely refuses at about 397 or above, not at 389. ADR 0083's revisit list (around line 774) already says staging must `SHOW max_connections` before the estimate can give way. An operator in an incident who compares the console count with 389 will draw the wrong line. The alarm text ('the 394 the connection budget reads') is accurate; only this sentence states the estimate as fact.
confirmed.fix: Say that 389 is the budget's lower bound, and that the instance's actual limit is `SHOW max_connections` (or the parameter group's value) less the 5 reserved, until staging's measured figure replaces the estimate in infra/lib/connections.ts.

refuted.title: A retried job that did not complete gets no codes in the summary
refuted.reason:
The facts in the finding are correct, but they don't show a defect these commits introduced. This round added a feature with a stated scope, and the code delivers exactly that scope. For failed jobs, the commits added information and took nothing away.

1. The scope is stated and the code matches it. Commit acad05cd says "The weekly run prints those codes beside a job that completed on a later attempt ... the check is unchanged". ADR 0083 says the same: "The weekly run prints those codes beside a job that completed on a later attempt, so the job log says why". So does the JOB_ATTEMPT_FAILED_MESSAGE doc comment in apps/worker/src/worker.ts. docs/runbooks/ci.md puts the codes under the bullet "A job completed on attempt 2 or 3". In tools/release-capacity/checks.ts verdict(), the `logged` clause is in the `job.attempts > 1` branch for a completed measured job, which is what that contract says.

2. The not-completed branch was not changed. `git diff 3ac856d5 c2626113 -- tools/release-capacity/checks.ts` has no added or removed line in the `job.state !== 'completed'` branch. That branch prints "ended <state>, not completed" exactly as it did at base.

3. Nothing got worse, and failed jobs gained information. Before these commits no attempt logged a code anywhere. Now run.ts attaches failedAttempts to every job with a job ID, including failed ones, and the full report is written to release-capacity.json. The reason line names the job's pg-boss ID, and every failed attempt now logs a `job attempt failed` line with that ID.

4. My test confirmed all of this. I ran a scratch vitest probe in my own clone at c2626113 (since removed). A price at state failed and at state retry, attempts 3, failedAttempts [DB_POOL_TIMEOUT x3], gave the reasons ["A price (price 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006) ended failed, not completed, in the concurrent phase", "the worker logged JOB_FAILED 1 times"]. The retry case gave the same with "ended retry". Without failedAttempts, the reason text was identical, which is the base behavior. The JSON round-trip of report() still carried jobs[A price].failedAttempts = ["DB_POOL_TIMEOUT","DB_POOL_TIMEOUT","DB_POOL_TIMEOUT"], while summary.md did not contain DB_POOL_TIMEOUT. The run still fails in every case.

What the finding describes is a reasonable request to extend the codes to failed and retry jobs, and it would make summary.md easier to read. But no code path behaves wrongly or against its own contract, and nothing regressed, so this is an enhancement rather than a real defect from this round's commits.

refuted.title: Neither the budget lines nor the reserve count the one-off tasks the runbooks tell operators to run
refuted.reason:
The facts the finding cites are true, but they don't add up to a defect. No reachable state makes the budget's verdict wrong, and the uncounted tasks fall outside a scope the code states openly.

How I checked: in my own clone at c2626113 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/e935a935-d2ff-5a27-860c-22677590c441/scratchpad/skp-infra3), I ran a throwaway vitest probe against connectionBudget and workerTaskPools. I then deleted it and the tree is clean.

1. The scope is declared, not miscounted. The first sentence at connections.ts:9-12 says "every task the environment can run at once", but the bullet at connections.ts:14-15 defines what is counted: each service at desired count x DEPLOY_MAX_HEALTHY_PERCENT, plus the migration task. ADR 0083's "As built" list says the same. RESERVE_CONNECTIONS (connections.ts:63-67) names exactly what it covers: 7 rotation functions and 3 for a person's session. It never claims to cover hand-run tasks, so "the platform rerun alone exceeds the reserve" compares the rerun to something it was never meant to fit in. The same commit's incident-response.md step 2 names "a task someone started by hand" as a known cause the DatabaseConnections alarm can see. The gap is acknowledged.

2. Outside a deploy, the hand-run tasks already fit inside the counted headroom. With platform desired at 1, the platform line counts 2 x 12, so a hand-run platform task (operator 2 + pg-boss 10, apps/worker/src/pools.ts:43-44) brings it to exactly the counted 2 tasks. With worker desired at 1, the worker line counts 2 x 25, so evaluate-permitted's openPool(worker.databaseUrl, 2) (permitted-cli.ts:45) fits in the second task's 25. Going over the stated worst case needs a hand-run that overlaps a deploy of every service at once.

3. Even in that case nothing changes. The probe printed production 205 (not 207 as the finding says; connections.test.ts EXPECTED and ADR 0083 also say 205), plus 12 plus 2 = 219. That is against 389 available (184 to spare) and under the alarm's 316. Dev and staging come to 163 + 14 = 177 against 389.

4. Both runbook passages are older than this round. restore-drill.md:38-39 dates from 25827685 (2026-10-17) and model-evaluation.md:142 from 388f213c (2026-10-26). This round only added a budget whose stated scope leaves them out.

At most the opening sentence of the docstring is broader than the bullet that defines it. That is a wording nit no test can show to fail, not a defect introduced by acad05cd, 5b7f5f83 or 068e8ed1.

refuted.title: attemptErrorCode passes through any upper-snake code an error carries, including identifier shapes the repo's own lints refuse
refuted.reason:
Refuted as a defect. The mechanics are right, but nothing can reach them, and no rule is broken.

1. Confirmed in my clone at c2626113. I copied attemptErrorCode exactly as written (apps/worker/src/worker.ts:126-145) into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/e935a935-d2ff-5a27-860c-22677590c441/scratchpad/skp-secrt1-probe/probe.ts and ran it with node 24. { code: 'MBR123456789' } returns MBR123456789 and { code: 'SMITH_JOHN' } returns SMITH_JOHN, through the line-138 branch /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,62}$/. The logger's allowlistedFields checks only keys and primitive types.

2. Nothing reaches it, and the finding admits this. I checked every place a code is set in apps/worker/src and packages/*/src:
   - EdiError codes are the fixed EDI_ERROR_CODES enum. EdiError is a data record, not something thrown, and its messages are built from fixed codes (errors.ts:1-18).
   - These are fixed constants or enums: ContentFailureCode, RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH, ReconciliationRefusal, EXPORT_HELD.
   - PacketRuleError takes a SQLSTATE or the literal '23514'/'22007' (services.ts:81, 449-761). These start with a digit, fail line 138, and log as PACKET_RULE_ERROR.
   - BillingProviderError codes are lowercase Stripe or simulator codes, which fail the upper-case regex.
   - pg errors log as DB_<SQLSTATE>, and Node system errors as E*/ERR_*.
   - The worker's other dependencies (AWS SDK v3, pg-boss, yauzl, zod) put no document data in a lowercase string `code`.
   No path turns 835, contract or export content into an error's `code`. What remains is a guess about some future error class, not a reproducible defect.

3. No lint or guard it cites is violated. tools/lint-logs/scan.ts NINE_DIGITS (scan.ts:21, 82) checks only string literals in log calls in the source, not values computed at runtime. packages/observability phi-guard.ts says it guards URLs, S3 keys and job payloads, not log fields.

4. Filtering by shape is already how this codebase does it, from before this round. At base 3ac856d5, screeningRunFailureCode accepts /^[A-Z0-9_]{1,32}$/, which takes 'MBR123456789' too. It is logged for every screening run at screening/thread.ts:59. models/permitted.ts:348 uses the same filter. attemptErrorCode's doc comment states this rule ("a code the error carries in this codebase's form or Node's"), and the code matches it.

At most, the suggested allowlist or nine-digit refusal is optional hardening. It is not a defect these commits introduced, and no test can show one being reached.
